title: Audit the stacked 11520 KAIOS warp ATM lineage without importing custody, payment, contracts, or writable automation
reason: PR 203 is stacked on held PR 200, is 720 commits behind exact current main, and combines a second trading stack with real-asset escrow, custody, single-oracle PnL clearing, wallet signing, Mainnet addresses, and inherited write-token automation. Its exact head fails closed only because deployment addresses are null; populating them would enable approvals and real transactions. These protected effects and unresolved security properties cannot be merged by this automation. The only safe bounded task is an evidence-only lineage audit that changes no candidate Runtime, UI, workflow, contract, authority, or pull-request state.
blocking_findings: PR 203 is stacked on held PR 200 rather than exact current main and is 720 commits behind the current product and safety architecture.
The inherited workflow exposes schedule and workflow_dispatch, grants actions:write and contents:write, pushes directly to main, and dispatches Pages.
The ATM contract permits arbitrary token pairs despite receiving a KAIOS constructor address and does not account for fee-on-transfer or rebasing assets.
The margin vault creates a duplicate real KAIOS custody ledger and credits requested amounts instead of observed balance deltas.
The clearing contract trusts one administrator-controlled mutable oracle and lacks quorum, deviation bounds, round IDs, replay protection, and a market allowlist.
Clearing reserve funding has no provider-share, redemption, or ownership accounting while the contract can custody and transfer real KAIOS.
The quote router trusts caller-supplied Life and wallet identifiers, uses JavaScript Number arithmetic for token amounts, and lacks allowlisted oracle provenance and decimal normalization.
The wallet bridge embeds BSC Mainnet addresses and would send approvals and transactions once contract addresses are populated; it hardcodes 18 decimals.
The standalone warp UI loads third-party code and public market/RPC endpoints and has no current V4.1 Game, Responsive, or direct 390x844 screenshot evidence.
The exact-head EVM tests use well-behaved mock tokens and do not cover malicious or fee-on-transfer tokens, oracle manipulation, reserve redemption, upgrade/storage safety, or deployment provenance.
safe_successor_requirements: Start from exact current main on a non-codex branch and reuse the current native-market and authenticated-actor architecture instead of adding a parallel exchange core.
Keep Mainnet addresses, signing, custody, payment, allowance, transfer, settlement, and chain mutation disconnected until exact Human authority and security review exist.

If contract work is separately authorized, enforce exact asset allowlists, balance-delta accounting, reentrancy-safe token handling, emergency exits, reserve ownership/redemption, and adversarial token tests.
Use repository-bound oracle provenance with freshness, decimal normalization, deviation limits, round identity, replay resistance, and an independently reviewed trust model.
Build any retained UI inside current V4.1 and pass exact-head Universal, Game, Responsive, functional Chromium, and direct 390x844 screenshot inspection.
